criteria.name: Names a specific customer and a specific future state, not a platitude
criteria.rationale: Customer is named down to the individual and constraint set: "Dr. Hana Lindqvist, who runs a six-person academic lab on a four-year grant and needs a benchtop centrifuge this quarter," with the $11k price consuming her whole equipment line. The future state is equally concrete — "maintenance history is attached to its serial number and visible before she commits" and she buys "in an afternoon at a third of the price of new." Neither reads as an interchangeable platitude.

criteria.name: Commits to at least one grounding factor (insight, trend, or technology bet)
criteria.rationale: It commits to a named insight — "The reason used lab equipment doesn't sell is provenance, not price" — and pairs it with a trend claim that "service contracts on this class of instrument have gone almost entirely digital and manufacturer-held in the last few years." It then states the bet explicitly and names two conditions under which it is wrong, which is well below the "make lives better" altitude.

criteria.name: Something a reader could point to and say "this didn't happen"
criteria.rationale: The pivot trigger is measurable and time-bounded: "If a few hundred provenance-verified units are listed and they don't sell measurably faster, or for measurably more, than the same models with no service history, the premise is wrong… runnable within a year." It specifies a control group (same models, no service history), so a reader could unambiguously observe the failure.

criteria.name: Vision Statement swap-test
criteria.rationale: "Every used lab instrument carries a verifiable service history, so PIs buy refurbished by default" binds to a specific mechanism (verifiable service history), a specific buyer (PIs), and a specific outcome (refurbished as default). An incumbent used-equipment marketplace competing on inventory or price could not swap its name in without contradicting its own model, since the statement asserts provenance rather than price is the unlock.

criteria.name: Future State swap-test
criteria.rationale: The future state is mechanism-bound rather than aspirational: "The unit's actual maintenance history is attached to its serial number and visible before she commits." A competitor without access to manufacturer-held digital service records cannot claim this scene, and the closing consequence — "Equipment stops being scrapped at the end of every grant cycle" — is downstream of that same specific mechanism.

criteria.name: Why Us / Why Now extended swap-test
criteria.rationale: The "why us" is non-transferable founder-specific evidence — "Five years as a field service engineer for a major instrument manufacturer, having personally opened several thousand of these machines" — and it converts that into a concrete edge: knowing "which fields matter, which are theatre, and where records lie." The "why now" rests on the recent digital-service-record shift that "nobody has built on top of it yet"; the dating ("in the last few years") is the weakest phrasing in the artifact, but the combined claim still breaks under both swaps.
